children: Shares of Aequs Ltd. are in focus on Tuesday, October 13, after the company announced long-term supply agreements with Safran for aerospace applications.
With this, Aequs said it now has relationships with six entities of Safran.
The precision manufacturing company informed the exchanges on Monday regarding it signing the agreements with Safran, which is a global leader in the aerospace industry for critical components.
The contracts will support Safran's supply chain and ongoing production programs, while also contribute to the growth and development of Aequs within the aerospace sector, it said.

The company said the agreements build on its longstanding engagements with Safran Landing Systems with new contracts and also extends the relationship to other Safran entities, such as Safran AeroSystems and Safran Electronics & Defense.

Aequs said that the agreements involve major work being carried out at the upcoming Aequs Engine Components Ecosystem (AECE) in Hosur, Tamil Nadu. The awards cover the machining of superalloys parts, the supply of complex machine coating and assembly of landing gear components for the Airbus A320, A330, A350 and Boeing 787 programs, it said.

Aequs will leverage its integrated aerospace manufacturing ecosystem and end-to-end capabilities across forging, precision machining, special processes, surface treatments, and assembly to manufacture these products.

The agreements further strengthen the role of its Belagavi Aerospace Cluster as an integrated manufacturing base serving global aerospace supply chains, the filing stated. This base will be further expanded with the upcoming AECE in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, where the manufacture of all medium and large parts will be taken up, it added.

Aequs chairman and CEO Aravind Melligeri said the components the company will manufacture for Safran are among the most demanding flight-critical products to industrialise. "These landmark awards further demonstrate the depth of aerospace manufacturing capability now available in India and the strength of the ecosystem we have created," he said.

The exchange filing added that the announcement comes close on the heels of the agreement inked between Aequs and Safran Landing Systems in July 2026 to supply fully assembled A320 family aircraft wheels.

The July agreement is Aequs' first serial production agreement extending beyond 15 years, through 2042, and will see complete aircraft wheels manufactured entirely in India, from Indian-sourced aluminum to the final assembly and testing, creating a 100% in-country manufacturing value addition, it added.
Aequs shares ended the previous session 2.7% lower at ₹266 per share. The stock has increased 20% in the past month and is up 92.5% this year, so far.

title: Aequs shares in focus after securing long-term supply agreements with Safran
